title: Support playbook + customer-facing docs for new 429 semantics (priority routing/quotas)
creator: Talia Benson
body:
Context
We’re rolling out hot-route capacity protection (tier-aware quotas/rate limits + priority routing + admission control) across Hosted API + Dedicated. This changes what customers see when they hit enforcement, especially 429s. Support needs a consistent story, macros, and an escalation path for enterprise complaints (e.g., “we’re paying for SLA but see 429s”).

Scope of this ticket
1) Support-facing “Known issues & workarounds” doc explaining:
- What changed and why (fleet health + enterprise SLO preservation)
- 429 reason codes and what they mean
- Required headers/payload fields (what Support should ask customers to share)
- Recommended retry/backoff guidance
- When it’s expected vs when to escalate

2) Zendesk macros (templates) for common 429 cases:
- Quota/rate limit exceeded
- Overload shedding/admission control
- Streaming termination under shed
- Enterprise complaints requesting exception / higher burst

3) Escalation path + internal checklist:
- What data to collect
- Which team to page (SRE vs Platform vs Routing)
- Which dashboards/runbooks to link
- How to request a temporary exception (guardrails + approvers)

4) Ensure alignment with public docs updates (redwood-docs) and error payload copy.

Deliverables / Links
- Confluence (Support): sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/enterprise-priority-429-and-quota-behavior.json
- Public docs PR: sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-2217-document-429-reason-codes-and-retry-guidance.json
- 429 reason codes PR (gateway): sources/github/redwood/pr-27441-add-overload-reason-codes-to-429-responses.json
- Runbook (SRE): sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/runbook-overload-protection-and-admission-control.json
- Dashboard spec (SRE): sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/dashboard-spec-hot-route-protection.json

Proposed (and implemented) 429 taxonomy for Support
Support should classify 429s using reason code + headers:
- reason=quota_exceeded: customer exceeded allotted quota window for their plan/tier. Expected; advise backoff + request quota increase via Sales/CS if sustained.
- reason=rate_limited: customer exceeded short-window RPS/token budget (bursty). Expected; advise jittered exponential backoff + client-side concurrency caps.
- reason=overload_shed: fleet/route under pressure and request was intentionally shed to protect higher-priority budgets. Expected for best-effort traffic during overload. For enterprise traffic: escalate if sustained or violates stated SLO.
- reason=admission_control: routing admission control is active; best-effort gated earlier. Similar handling to overload_shed.
- reason=tier_policy: request blocked by policy (route not permitted for tier, or route-group rule). Not overload; route customer to correct tier/contract config.

Headers/payload fields Support should ask for
- x-request-id (or redwood-request-id)
- x-redwood-retry-after-ms (preferred), and/or Retry-After
- x-redwood-429-reason (string reason code)
- x-redwood-route-group (e.g., chat.completions, embeddings, rerank)
- x-redwood-tier (best_effort / enterprise)
- timestamp + region

Retry guidance (Support-safe summary)
- Always implement jittered exponential backoff.
- Respect Retry-After / x-redwood-retry-after-ms when present.
- For streaming clients: treat mid-stream shed as a retryable termination; do not “spin” immediately—wait at least the provided retry-after.

Escalation criteria (enterprise)
Escalate to on-call if ANY of the below:
- Customer is in enterprise tier AND reports sustained 429s > 5 minutes on protected routes (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank) in a single region.
- 429 reason is overload_shed/admission_control AND customer claims impact to production SLO.
- Any report of increased 5xx or p95/p99 regression correlated with 429 spikes.

Escalation checklist
1) Confirm reason code + headers above.
2) Check dashboards: “Hot route protection overview” (tier split + shed rate + latency burn).
3) Confirm if protection is active (incident-bot messages) and whether this is expected shedding of best-effort.
4) If enterprise is impacted: page SRE (Rafael Mendes / Aisha Bello) and tag Platform (Ethan Park) + Routing (Mina Haddad) in #incidents thread.
5) For exception requests (higher burst): route via TAM/CS (Liam O’Rourke / Rachel Kim) and Solutions Eng (Markus Klein). Require:
- time-bound exception
- max burst cap
- region scope
- explicit rollback conditions

Acceptance criteria
- Confluence Support doc is published and linked from internal Support index.
- Zendesk macros created and reviewed by Support lead (Dev Patel) and PM (Nikhil Sharma).
- Public docs PR merged and matches Support doc (same reason codes + headers).
- Escalation path validated in at least one on-call exercise / real incident thread (or game day).

Notes
This ticket does not change enforcement logic; it documents and operationalizes it. Any mismatches found between observed 429 payloads and docs should be filed as follow-up bugs against gateway/routing.
comments: 2025-12-09 (Talia Benson): Creating this as a gating item for GA. We’ve had repeated confusion in Support about “quota vs overload” and enterprise expectations. Wei to draft, Dev to review, Nikhil to sign off on customer-facing framing.
2025-12-11 (Wei Chen): First draft of Support doc is in progress. Need final list of reason codes/headers from Amara (gateway) and Jordan (policy engine).

2025-12-12 (Amara Diallo): Current gateway emits x-redwood-429-reason and x-redwood-retry-after-ms behind feature flag. Reason codes implemented: quota_exceeded, rate_limited, overload_shed. Routing adds admission_control in next PR. Please avoid documenting any header names that aren’t stable yet—will confirm by EOW.

2025-12-16 (Dev Patel): Added requests for macros to include: (1) ‘expected best-effort throttling’ language and (2) an enterprise-specific version that immediately asks for request IDs + timestamps + region. Also please include a one-liner on why “retry loops” worsen throttling.

2025-12-18 (Nikhil Sharma): For customer messaging, prefer “capacity protection” framing over “priority” where possible. We can mention enterprise traffic is ‘protected’ without implying strict ‘always admitted’ guarantees. Escalation criteria for enterprise should reference contractual SLA (route-specific).

2025-12-23 (Wei Chen): Support doc updated with final header names and reason codes (including admission_control and tier_policy). Added section: ‘When NOT to escalate’ (best-effort, overload_shed during regional pressure).

2026-01-07 (Owen Phillips): Ran through macros with Support team. Request: include a short ‘copy/paste’ snippet asking customers to include relevant response headers (some customers only paste status code).

2026-01-10 (Elliot Price): Public docs PR updated to align with Support doc terminology; ensured examples show structured 429 payload + headers. Waiting on final approval from PM and SRE for retry guidance wording.

2026-01-15 (Rafael Mendes): During game day we saw customers might confuse quota_exceeded vs overload_shed since both are 429. Recommend Support doc emphasize reason code is source of truth; dashboards show shed rate separately. Approved escalation flow.
2026-01-22 (Wei Chen): All deliverables done: Confluence doc published, macros created, public docs PR merged. Marking Done.
